The main objection came from Speaker C (User Interface Designer), who said a beeper-style finder would be technically difficult because an infrared signal cannot reach a remote lost under the settee, and that it might be just a gimmick.

answers.answer: Speaker D (Marketing Expert) raised repetitive strain injury (RSI) in the second meeting, saying people who change channels too often may hurt their wrists, and buttons were implicated. The team responded by asking for ergonomics and medical research, consulting legal, and suggesting lower or flat buttons or touch input; the final design became a rubber, double-curved remote with simple push-buttons that the team marketed as anti-RSI (Speaker A, Project Manager, noted in the third meeting that any button is still repetitive).

answers.answer: Team TS3003 settled on customers aged sixty to eighty, narrowing an earlier "forty plus" group, mainly because the trend research for that group showed older buyers wanted familiar shapes, dark colours and wood, and the team wanted a simple, few-button remote with teletext and large subtitles for them. Speaker A (Project Manager) argued the forty-plus market was broad, and Speaker D (Marketing Expert) had pushed for younger customers, so the group chose the narrower older segment. In the final meeting, Speaker D questioned this and proposed refocusing on younger people, but that was left open.

brief:
Brief for Team TS3012 before meeting TS3012d (based on TS3012a, TS3012b, TS3012c).

WHAT HAS BEEN DECIDED (CURRENT)
- Speech recognition is now included in the deluxe design, reversing the earlier decision not to implement it, because the new component is small and people want it. [TS3012c: "That's small. So we can implement it. So why why if it's small and we can imp why shouldn't we?"]
- The LCD screen is included in the deluxe edition, since the team is moving towards deluxe because that is what people want. [TS3012c: "I think we'll I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want."]
- The case material is rubber, which is durable against falls and suits the young target group's wish for a spongy feel; wood is not an option. [TS3012c: "The case, it will be the material will be rubber, suppose."] [TS3012c: "No, wood i wood's not an option. Well it it's stylish, but we can yeah, but you can change your covers anyway."]
- A beep and a flashing light are implemented to help recover a lost remote. [TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote."]
- The most used functions, such as zapping, sit where the thumb rests; in the deluxe layout the number keys move below. [TS3012c: "For zapping, cau because people are zapping most of the time."]
- The energy source is regular batteries; kinetic and solar options were dropped and no rechargeable module is offered. [TS3012c: "Uh energy, we choose regular regular batteries. The chip is advanced because we have the advanced features."] [TS3012c: "Well, mm it's not in the list. So we cannot choose from it. So"]
- The product keeps focusing on younger people, which was the main goal. [TS3012c: "We're definitely focussing on the younger people, 'cause that was our main goal."]
- The remote has a leaner shape with softened corners and a rounded top, instead of sharp Star Trek-like edges. [TS3012c: "I think so because it looks leaner and we should just go with that."]

WHAT CHANGED ALONG THE WAY
- Speech recognition went from not implemented (too immature, too much memory, multiple languages) to included in the deluxe design because the component is now small and people want it. [TS3012b: "I don't think it should be implemented in a remote control yet uh."] [TS3012c: "That's small. So we can implement it. So why why if it's small and we can imp why shouldn't we?"]
- The LCD screen went from a proposal to include it only if affordable to being included in the deluxe edition as customers want it. [TS3012b: "if it's not too expensive, we should include it"] [TS3012c: "I think we'll I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want."]
- Changeable covers went from a proposal to sell a basic remote with separately bought covers to being left out of the basic design, possibly added later for fashion. [TS3012b: "So you don't have to I think you don't have to make entire remote controls."] [TS3012c: "If we wanna expand our options, f be fashionable, then we can get changeable covers."]
- The lost-remote aid went from a flashing LED for deaf users to a beep plus flashing light. [TS3012b: "Perhaps we should also make uh something like a flash on it, if you if it's lost, for people that are deaf."] [TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote."]
- Advanced TV functions went from a second-level menu on the remote to navigation through the LCD screen menu, with no button per function. [TS3012b: "maybe a second second level menu for the advanced things."] [TS3012c: "the advanced option could also be integrated in the L_C_D_ screen, of course, because you don't have to have a button for everything."]
- The remote shape went from a distinct shape with more curves to a leaner shape with softened corners and a rounded top. [TS3012b: "I think it should be a little distinct from everything else"] [TS3012c: "I think so because it looks leaner and we should just go with that."]

OPEN ACTIONS AND OWNERS
- Speaker B (User Interface Designer) and Speaker C (Industrial Designer) work together on the final internal and external design, and Speaker D (Marketing Expert) finds out how the product will fit the market. [TS3012c: "apparently you guys, you should work together on the final design, both on internal and external design."]
- Speaker D (Marketing Expert) will look up the exact percentage of people who want voice recognition. [TS3012c: "Yeah. Mean of uh seventy percent I think. Uh I'm I have to look it up."]
- Speaker C (Industrial Designer) will find out whether a docking or recharging solution is possible and what it costs. [TS3012b: "Yes. I'm going to try to find that out."]
- Speaker A (Project Manager) will research whether the remote can operate the TV's advanced menu, since most TV menu buttons are shared between brands. [TS3012b: "we need to put some research into that if if we can open the menu"]
- Speaker C (Industrial Designer) is studying materials for cost, assuming standard fibreglass circuit board and copper wiring, with integrated parts being cheaper. [TS3012b: "Uh material study, I'm working on that um for the the costs."]
- Everyone should think of a product name rather than a vague serial number. [TS3012b: "let's give this uh a name, and not like some vague serial number that no one understands"]

DISAGREEMENTS AND QUESTIONS STILL OPEN
- The corporate colour and slogan are unsettled: C wants a yellow remote with black buttons, B prefers a neutral base colour because of covers, and A leans to black and yellow. [TS3012c: "It's either black cover with yellow buttons or vice versa."]
- Where to place the speech recognition microphone (top, side, or double) is still open, and the transmitter location may cause interference. [TS3012c: "Um yeah, it could be either be here or make a double microphone."]
- A objects to the kinetic energy option because remotes lie still most of the time, so there is not enough movement to generate power. [TS3012c: "I'm sure t I mean remotes lie still I think like ninety nine percent of the time."]
- It is unclear whether customers value a rechargeable battery and would pay extra for it. [TS3012b: "I'm not sure, you should find out if it's if rechargeable is important."]
- Budget is tight, according to the User Interface Designer, which conflicts with the selling price target. [TS3012a: "Okay, well that's not that much to work with."]
- Whether the remote should be usable by disabled people is unresolved, since truly disabled users may be a problem. [TS3012a: "Do we want people who are disabled in any way to uh, yeah, to be able to use it as well?"]
